PHASE 105 IMPLEMENTATION REPORT: Automated Recovery + PG Persistence + DLQ Alerting

## Summary
Upgraded Queue API to v2.0 with PostgreSQL persistence, automated task recovery on container startup, and DLQ alerting. Addresses all GPT-4o Phase 104 findings: Critical (automated recovery), High (PG persistence), Medium (DLQ alerting).

## Components Built

### 1. PostgreSQL Persistence for Queue Tasks
- asyncpg connection pool (min 2, max 10, 30s command timeout)
- queue_tasks table: 13 columns (id, agent_id, agent_name, status, capability, priority, input_data JSONB, output_data JSONB, error, latency_ms, retry_count, max_retries, created_at, updated_at)
- 2 indexes: idx_queue_tasks_status, idx_queue_tasks_agent
- persist_task(): INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE (upsert)
- get_pending_tasks(): SELECT pending tasks ordered by priority DESC, created_at ASC
- cleanup_old_queue_tasks(): DELETE completed/failed/cancelled/timeout tasks older than N days
- Connection retry: 3 attempts, 2s delay between attempts
- Graceful fallback: in-memory only if PG unavailable

### 2. Automated Recovery on Startup
- @app.on_event('startup'): initializes PG pool, sets persistence callback, queries pending tasks, calls execution_queue.recover_from_persistence()
- Recovery runs automatically when container starts
- Logs: 'Auto-recovered N pending tasks on startup' or 'No pending tasks to recover'
- Verified in production: pg_connected: true, queue starts empty (no pending tasks to recover)
- Manual recovery endpoint also available: POST /queue/recover?limit=100

### 3. DLQ Alerting System
- DLQAlertConfig: webhook_url, email_recipient, min_severity, rate_limit_seconds
- send_dlq_alert(): sends structured alert (event, task_id, error, agent_id, timestamp, severity)
- Rate limiting: max 1 alert per 60 seconds (configurable)
- Log-based alerting (always active): structured log warning on every DLQ entry
- Webhook alerting (optional): HTTP POST to configured webhook URL
- DLQ add wrapped with alerting: _dlq_add_with_alert() fires alert on every DLQ entry
- Alert config endpoints: GET/POST /dlq/alerts/config

### 4. New API Endpoints
- POST /queue/recover: manual task recovery from PG
- POST /queue/retention/{days}: delete old completed/failed tasks
- GET /dlq/alerts/config: get alert configuration
- POST /dlq/alerts/config: set alert configuration (webhook_url, min_severity, rate_limit_seconds)

### 5. Tests (test_queue_api_v2.py, 23 tests)
TestQueueAPIV2 (10 tests): health with pg_connected, queue_stats with pg_connected, submit, get_task, nonexistent, list_tasks, cancel, cancel_nonexistent, recover endpoint, retention endpoint

TestDLQAPIV2 (6 tests): stats, list, add_and_get, remove, clear, requeue

TestDLQAlerting (7 tests): get_alert_config, set_alert_config, alert_rate_limiting, send_dlq_alert_no_webhook, persist_task_no_pg, get_pending_tasks_no_pg, cleanup_no_pg

## Test Results
- 542 passed, 7 skipped (up from 536)
  - +23 v2.0 tests (replaced 17 v1.0 tests, net +6)
  - 519 existing tests
- 24 Docker containers running
- PG persistence confirmed connected in production (pg_connected: true)
- Automated recovery active on container startup

## Key Achievements
- Addressed GPT-4o Phase 104 Critical: Automated recovery on startup ✓
- Addressed GPT-4o Phase 104 High: PG persistence for queue tasks ✓
- Addressed GPT-4o Phase 104 Medium: DLQ alerting system ✓
- PostgreSQL persistence with upsert (INSERT ON CONFLICT)
- Rate-limited alerts (max 1 per 60s)
- Retention cleanup endpoint
- 542 tests passing, zero failures

## Known Limitations
- Queue not yet integrated with agent execution API (standalone)
- No WebSocket support for real-time monitoring
- Real execution tests still skipped
- DLQ alerting webhook not tested end-to-end
- No task TTL (tasks persist indefinitely without retention)

## Questions for GPT-4o
1. Should we integrate the async queue with the existing agent execution API (replace synchronous execution)?
2. Should we add WebSocket support for real-time queue monitoring?
3. What should be the next priority: real execution tests with API keys, OS-level network isolation, or video providers?
4. Should we add a scheduled retention job (auto-cleanup) instead of manual endpoint?
